tldr: Admins can now export all family data as a ZIP file. A background job writes 4 CSV files and an NDJSON file and attaches the ZIP to a FamilyExport record.
goal: Let a family take a full copy of its data out of Maybe.

story.heading: Family::DataExporter added
story.body: It writes accounts, transactions, trades and categories as CSV, plus all.ndjson, into a ZIP.

story.heading: Settings starts an export; a job builds the ZIP
story.body: The controller creates a FamilyExport and queues FamilyDataExportJob. The job sets processing, then completed, or failed on an error.

story.heading: FamilyExport added
story.body: A new family_exports table stores the status. Family has many exports. The ZIP is an Active Storage file.

story.heading: Settings lists the last 10 exports to download
story.body: A Turbo frame refreshes the list every 3 seconds while an export runs. download sends the file only when the export is completed.

story.heading: The whole change
story.body: Web endpoints start the export, Background jobs call Family::DataExporter, and a FamilyExport record holds the status and the file.

components.summary: Settings shows an Export data button and a list of exports that refreshes while one runs.
New FamilyExportsController: admins start an export, list the last 10 and download a completed one.
New FamilyExport with a status and a file; new Family::DataExporter writes 4 CSV files and all.ndjson into a ZIP.
New FamilyDataExportJob builds the ZIP, attaches it and sets the export status.

decisions.title: Build the archive in a background job
decisions.why: A full export reads every account and transaction. The request returns at once and the UI polls for the result.
decisions.alternative: Build and stream the ZIP inside the request.

decisions.title: Exporter in the Family:: namespace
decisions.why: The app keeps domain logic in model namespaces. Family::DataExporter follows that convention.

decisions.title: A FamilyExport record holds the state
decisions.why: The list, the polling and the download read a single status. The file is an Active Storage attachment on the record.
decisions.alternative: Keep the state only in the job queue.

decisions.title: CSV per entity plus an NDJSON dump
decisions.why: The CSV import of Maybe reads the CSV files back. NDJSON keeps each record with its nested data, such as the accountable of an account.
decisions.alternative: A single JSON document for everything.
